description: The filter and envelopes of an acid bass synthesiser, without the oscillator: patch a tone into it and gate it, and it gives you the sweep, the accent and the squelch

params.text: Sets the resting corner frequency of the filter, from 40Hz to 4500Hz
Sets how far the filter envelope sweeps the corner, reaching five octaves at its maximum; about a third of the sweep is below the resting frequency and the rest above it
Sets the resonance, from none to 125 per cent, past which the filter squeals on every note
Sets how much louder and brighter an accented note is than a plain one, from a quarter to all of the available accent
Sets how long the filter envelope takes to fall, from 200ms to 2 seconds
Scales what the cutoff jack adds, 5V covering the whole cutoff range at its maximum
Scales what the resonance jack adds, 5V covering the whole resonance range at its maximum
Scales what the decay jack adds, 5V covering the whole decay range at its maximum
Scales what the sweep jack adds, 5V covering the whole sweep range at its maximum
Switches the gate jack between being read as a gate, where releasing it ends the note, and as a trigger, where the note runs its decay out whatever the jack does

inputs.text: A rising edge starts a note; whether its falling edge ends one depends on the GATE/TRIG button
A note is accented when this jack is at 1V or more as its gate begins, or if it arrives during the attack
The oscillator tone to be filtered; the maker expects peaks no higher than 7V, above which accented notes hard clip
Adds to the resting corner frequency, scaled by its attenuator
Adds to the resonance, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between none and 125 per cent
Adds to the filter envelope's fall time, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between 200ms and 2 seconds
Adds to the sweep depth, scaled by its attenuator, with the total clamped between none and five octaves

outputs.text: The filtered and enveloped note, with its DC removed and hard clipped at ±12V

notes: this module makes no sound on its own: it needs a tone patched into OSC and a gate, and the accent jack is separate from the gate.
mono only: a polyphonic cable is read as its first channel and the output carries one channel.
the upper row of four lamps follows the filter envelope through attack, sustain, decay and ended, and the row below it follows the amplitude envelope the same way.
the sustain lamp of each envelope row is never lit; neither envelope has a sustain stage.
the blue lamp is lit while the current note is accented, and the two small lamps beside the button show whether the gate jack is being read as a gate or as a trigger.
the accent lengthens and deepens the filter envelope rather than being an envelope of its own, which is why turning the resonance up makes accents bite harder.
the corner frequency is held between 16Hz and 18000Hz however far the envelope and the CV try to push it.
the four large knobs each draw a gold arc from their own position round to where their CV jack and attenuator have moved them.
menu: Oversample x2 — runs the filter at twice the sample rate, which is where the module starts
Oversample x4 — runs the filter at four times the sample rate
ENVMOD Octaves mode — sweeps the corner in octaves, the way the original does, rather than in hertz; with it off the ENVMOD knob is read as a span in hertz and its tooltip changes to match
